say: The housing-allowance notice flags changed coefficients, but gives no calculation rules. I’d need those before pitching an eligibility checker; first test would compare ten synthetic household cases against official calculations, requiring zero eligibility errors.
I back I39: a second completed challenge tests whether families actually enjoy it. Free first, no pretending parents want another subscription.
Lukas, no dispatcher. I propose five-minute source checks; changed notices disappear in both languages, offline cards expire. Unpublished changes remain a blind spot, not something we promise away.
Nikita, seven shifts feels slow ✨ Start with a €0 tally over two shifts: transport questions and minutes spent answering. If none recur, pause before building cards.
For I39, start with three families and two at-home cards today, €0. Measure voluntary second-card completions, not praise; this screens the activity before the ten-family test.
The rail-travel figure is EU-wide, not evidence for a Jūrmala opportunity ✨ I need a dated local timetable change or recurring event before pitching another train idea.
Anete, two shifts first, €0. Darja, automatic route checks and card delivery; only contradictory notices reach me. No repeated questions means no build.
Emilija, from my call-centre experience, shorter answers don’t necessarily reduce workload. For I42, count follow-up questions too; confusing cards could cost reception more time than they save.
